items.title: Single-block precision: the literal formula (4)

source.anchor: Equation (4); Appendix B.3 single-block paragraph through equation (26)
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: In the Section 3.1 standing construction, fix kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d, and for O in the real orthogonal group O(n) define A_O = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), as equation (4). This item covers the literal single-block formula, not the full block diagonal.
assumptions: n is a natural number; κ is real.
O is an n by n real orthogonal matrix; both determinant signs are allowed.

bindings.boundary: Only the single-block equation (26). Full block diagonal assembly, Gaussian normalization, unique minimizer and both query-complexity lower bounds remain open.

assumption_deltas.source: Real orthogonal matrix, literal coefficients and full coordinate-vector quantifier.
assumption_deltas.lean: Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ; literal scalar/matrix formula; IsHermitian over ℝ and dotProduct.
assumption_deltas.reason: Real Hermitian means symmetric, and dotProduct v v is the Euclidean squared norm; no entrywise matrix order or Pi norm is used.

assumption_deltas.source: Section 3.1 uses kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d in ambient dimension d.
assumption_deltas.lean: The literal matrix-valued definition is total for every natural n and every real kappa; its regularity theorem retains n>=3 and kappa>=4.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is only the same algebraic expression on a larger carrier. No off-source fallback, spectral estimate outside the theorem range, or ambient block conclusion is asserted. Ambient n<=d belongs to the later block construction.

items.title: Orthogonality and Cauchy–Schwarz give the single-block spectral bounds

source.anchor: Equation (4); Appendix B.3 single-block paragraph through equation (26)
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: For n>=3 and kappa>=4 and every real orthogonal n by n matrix O, the matrix A_O = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T) is symmetric and every real n-vector v satisfies v^T v <= v^T A_O v <= kappa v^T v. This is the single-block part of Appendix B.3 through equation (26), not the subsequent full block construction or minimizer conclusion.
assumptions: n≥3 and κ≥4 are the standing range in Section 3.1.
O belongs to the full real orthogonal group O(n).
The bounds hold for every real coordinate vector, including zero.
